item.title: [New] Twelve more Graph permissions became grantable, among them UserCertificateIds.ReadWrite.All, which can bind a certificate to any user, and AdministrativeUnitMember.ReadWrite.All
item.description:
UserCertificateIds.ReadWrite.All lets an application rewrite certificateUserIds, the values certificate-based authentication uses to decide which user a certificate signs in as: where certificate-based authentication is enabled, an app holding it can point a certificate issued by a CA the tenant trusts at any account, a Global Administrator included (inferred from how CBA user binding works; Microsoft's text says only that it updates certificate user IDs). It is grantable in every tenant from today and documented nowhere, so no consent review checklist names it yet.

Graph · Add the GUIDs 10d0f892-6ef8-4cd8-9f4c-614345762e90 (application) and 01d92422-30dd-4401-a504-aa0a84c463bc (delegated) of UserCertificateIds.ReadWrite.All and 9205f977-63a7-4c23-9d0c-8051235b0e4c / 14f19140-a110-48da-b3ba-63c2862bb7da of AdministrativeUnitMember.ReadWrite.All to the consent alert list today; alert on any change to certificateUserIds in the audit log.

item.title: [New] From 4 November every default user can create agent blueprints unless 'Users can create agent blueprints' is set to No
item.description:
A default-on permission for every member user to create a new kind of workload identity widens the app-registration surface that consent-phishing and persistence techniques already abuse, and tenants that locked down app registration are not covered by that setting.

Entra · Decide before 4 November: set 'Users can create agent blueprints' to No unless there is a business case, keep Agent ID Developer as the delegated path, and add agent blueprint creation by non-admins to the app-registration detections.

item.title: [New] Entra stops auto-granting AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager to agent blueprints from 4 November; app-only agents that create their own identities need explicit admin consent or get 403
item.description:
Until now every agent blueprint could mint agent identities without any admin approval and without a visible grant. After the change that authority becomes an auditable, revocable app-role assignment, so the grant itself becomes something to monitor.

Entra · Before 4 November, filter the Entra audit log on ApplicationManagement / Add Service Principal where the initiator is an Application and the target an agent identity; grant AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager explicitly (from 16 October) only to the blueprints that need it, and alert on new grants of it afterwards.
